utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before beginning the hearing, I should like to say good afternoon to everyone here present, and I would like to ask Madam Registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. For the transcript, can we have the appearances, please. First for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. If it please the Court, Dirk Ryneveld, appearing today with my co-counsel, Daryl Mundis. And the Prosecution is prepared to proceed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Milenko Radovic, attorney from Foca Srbinje, appearing on behalf of the accused Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Judge Amin El Mahdi, Pre-Trial Judge for this case. I should like to refer to two orders: The first, whereby the President of the Tribunal has attributed this case to the first Trial Chamber; and the second order designating me by the Chamber as the Pre-Trial Judge. I should now like to address Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Stankovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do not hesitate to tell me if there should be any problem regarding sound or any other problem or if you wish to intervene, please do not hesitate to let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As you know, we are today having a hearing in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I know that there has been a request by the Defence in connection with the form of the indictment. A decision will probably be rendered in the next few days, but we would like to make progress without waiting for that ruling, because that would be in the interest of justice and above all in the interest of Mr. Stankovic himself. And I wish to say that as Pre-Trial Judge, it is my duty in the first place to make sure that the procedure is observed fully and that all matters which might arise can be addressed fairly. With your permission, I should like to address myself to the Prosecution. Where do we stand with respect to the disclosure in application of Rule 65?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can indicate to the Court that under Rule 66(A)(i) the supporting materials, of course, which had to be disclosed, those have in fact been disclosed to the accused. My understanding is that although on the 12th of July, I believe, that was the Initial Appearance, the accused appeared with different counsel. It became clear that he chose a different counsel, and the Prosecution was in correspondence with Mr. Radovic and due to Mr. Radovic's request, the supporting materials were actually provided to him after the 11th of August. Rather than send them to him through the normal mail, he wanted to come and pick them up. But it was at his request and I believe he acknowledges that he has received timely receipt of the supporting materials, although technically speaking it was 30 -- it was beyond 30 days, we were prepared to give it, but we wanted to comply with Defence counsel's request. With respect to the additional matters under 66(A)(ii), I can tell the Court that we have been streamlining this case. We have had to redact many of the materials that have been -- documents, et cetera, and statement which is were used in the trial of Kunarac et al. And we are almost at a position to be able to provide the Defence with additional material in full compliance with Rule 66(A)(ii), so we're well on the way to being able to fulfil our Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure obligations. I can also tell the Court that we've invited the Defence counsel to a meeting in our office immediately after this Status Conference in order to see how it is that we could perhaps efficiently speed up the process and collaboratively work out the pre-trial phase of this case. We are, of course, constantly aware of our Rule 68 obligations, and we are going to be disclosing any Rule 68 material that comes to our attention, as is our obligation. Those are my general comments, Your Honour, but we are fairly confident that this case can be streamlined. And I've asked Mr. Mundis, actually, to address you later with some particular matters. But since Your Honour has raised the issue of the challenge to the form of the indictment, and the fact that the Court is contemplating ruling on that matter in the next few days, I thought it only prudent to advise the Court that since Mr. Mundis and I have been assigned to this case, we have been looking at ways of streamlining the case, reducing the total number of witnesses, and we can also say that we have been reviewing the indictment itself, and it is possible that the Prosecution will actually be making an application to amend the indictment, to streamline it even further; however, we also anticipate that there could be three additional counts: Of rape, enslavement, and outrages upon personal indignity arising out of incidents concerning an individual by the pseudonym of DB in the period following her detention a the Karaman's house. So that is by way of, shall we say, an indication to the Court that that is what we are anticipating. And Mr. Mundis, I believe, will be addressing the topic later in the Status Conference if the Court would like to hear us on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. But I would like to make sure of one thing, however, and that is the following: You're saying that you're thinking of modifying yourself the indictment. I think that you responded to the request of the Defence, to the motion of the Defence, and I do not recollect that I read or that the Chamber was seized of your position, so this is an absolutely new position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely -- yes, absolutely correct, Your Honour. I became involved in this file after the filing of the response to which you refer. I might say that of course we cannot do this without leave of the Court, and this is the first opportunity that we have had in order to address the Court with respect to the potential that we may be seeking leave of this Court. And I thought it was only prudent to advise the Court of our contemplation of seeking leave to amend the indictment prior to the Court ruling necessarily on the form of the motion as it presently exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I seek a point of clarification. If I understand you correctly, you said that you have been in contact with the Defence counsel. Did you raise this issue among others, this issue of amendment to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- I can say -- what I've told the Court is that we have today invited Defence counsel to meet with us after the Status Conference. The only thing that Defence counsel knew is that we were inviting him to a meeting. One of the topics was going to be our proposed amendment to the indictment and other matters. So this has not been discussed with Defence counsel. He knew nothing about the meeting until moments prior to our 3:00 Status Conference. This is all very recent development.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for those clarifications. Can I now ask Defence counsel -- excuse me. Mr. Stankovic, did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I have to say at my Initial Appearance I was allotted -- designated an attorney. It wasn't somebody I had chosen of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand well, now the counsel that you have is a counsel of your choice, isn't it? The Defence counsel here present is a person of your choice?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this one. But the one at the Initial Appearance was officially designated. He wasn't my attorney. At my Initial Appearance, I didn't even ask for an attorney. I rejected the possibility of having one. So I'd like that to be quite clear. I wouldn't like to give the impression that I had one attorney at the Initial Appearance and then I decided to change him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Please don't speak so quickly because the interpreters have a hard time following you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I speak rather fast. It's part of my nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never mind. In any case, I can assure you that the Initial Appearance was before another Chamber, another Pre-Trial Judge, and today we are beginning, if I may put it that way, from scratch, from the beginning. So could I now ask the Defence counsel to address us, if he has anything to say, with regard to the disclosure of documents, witnesses, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what my learned friend opposite has said is quite right, that the Defence on the 26th of August at my own request received the indictment and the statements of 13 witnesses with the pseudonyms which were disclosed in accordance with Rule 66(A)(i). The Defence has up to now managed to study closely the amended indictment and the witness statements served on it. We have also been able to review a certain amount of documents linked to the issue of rape as processed by this Tribunal so far, as well as the appropriate literature, and we are continuing our efforts along those lines. The Defence, as you are aware, filed a motion against the indictment, and the Defence has also received the response of the Prosecution to this motion and submits that at this point in time there is no need for any position to be taken with respect to the allegations of the Prosecution. The Defence expects further disclosure of documents or any information to the effect that there is no more material to be disclosed by the Prosecution, upon which the Defence, after having received all the material pursuant to Rules 66(A)(ii), will be able to assess the time it will need for preparations for trial. I wish to point out that I have been appointed as Defence counsel for the accused Stankovic for a fixed term. And for the Defence to be able to continue its work in preparation of the case, it would be necessary for a decision to be taken on my designation for an unlimited term, in view of the fact that we have provided to the Registry all the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. necessary documentation for such a decision to be taken. The Defence will naturally pay attention to its obligations as emanating from Rule 67, of course, depending on the steps taken by the Prosecution. The Defence expects the Prosecution to act in accordance with Rule 68 and to provide us as soon as possible with all exculpatory material in its possession so that this, too, might be of assistance to us in preparing our case. The Defence will certainly do its best not to delay the proceedings unnecessarily and will do everything in its power to prepare the case for a fair and expeditious trial. Though this case in terms of its complexity has been ranked as at the highest level, from the standpoint of the Defence it is rather a complicated case and will certainly require some time for the Defence to collect Defence evidence, especially with regard to the identification and location of potential witnesses. And finally I should just like to point out that the Defence will within the deadlines fixed seek to fulfil all its obligations that Your Honour, as the Pre-Trial Judge, will assign on the Defence and especially its obligations emanating from paragraph G of Rule 65(F) and 73 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If I have understood you correctly, you have raised two questions: The first has to do with your final appointment as Defence counsel. Have you taken the necessary steps with the Registry to that end?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. And as I just pointed out, I have filed all the necessary documents for my appointment, as well as documents regarding the material position of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when was that? How long ago was that when you filed your request and the necessary documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I filed all those documents to the Registry on the 27th of August. However, one document linked to the property of my client, and before coming to The Hague I spoke to the financial inspector, Mr. Jovanovic, and my secretary yesterday forwarded that document as well, so that having mailed that document, the Defence has completed all the documents required for my appointment as permanent Defence counsel for Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that only recently you provided the document that was missing. Was that two days ago? A week ago? When was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the documents regarding me, myself, were filed on the 27th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I'm talking about the necessary document requested by the Registry concerning the financial status of Mr. Stankovic, if I understand you correctly. When did you submit that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the documents regarding Radovan Stankovic, the accused, were filed by me on the 27th of August, 2002, except for one document, which was required of me by the financial inspector and it has to do with the financial status of the accused and regarding his ownership of a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's precisely in connection with that document that I'm asking you. When did you submit that particular document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That document was faxed yesterday, according to what my secretary tells me. It was sent by fax to the Registry yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that Mr. Mundis wanted to raise a few issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I briefly rise to my feet simply to give the Trial Chamber through Your Honour as the Pre-Trial Judge a brief overview as to where the Prosecution or the approach the Prosecution seeks to take with respect to this case. I think that's helpful for planning purposes and will certainly benefit the Chamber as it attempts to deal with the pre-trial matters concerning this case. As Mr. Ryneveld has indicated, we will be meeting later this afternoon with Defence counsel Mr. Radovic. Among the issues that we anticipate will be raised during the course of that meeting would be potential grounds of agreement between the parties so that we can begin that process of attempting to narrow the issues which the Trial Chamber will be faced with. Perhaps in addition to any agreed-upon facts or in the event those discussions are not successful, the Prosecution will very shortly be filing a request pursuant to Rule 94(B), requesting the Trial Chamber to take judicial notice of certain adjudicated facts which were the result of the Kunarac trial and appeal. Given that the Kunarac case and the current case are closely linked, Your Honour, we will be filing a motion requesting for the Chamber to take judicial notice of certain adjudicated facts as established through the Appeals Chamber in the previous related case. In addition -- and of course also dependent upon any agreed upon facts which the parties are able to reach -- the Prosecution anticipates relying upon Rule 92 bis (D), whereby we will request the Trial Chamber to accept or to admit into evidence certain transcript evidence from the witnesses who testified in the Kunarac et al case. Once the Trial Chamber has addressed these two motions, which again we anticipate filing shortly, and of course having due regard for any agreed-upon facts which the parties may or may not be able to reach, the Prosecution would then be in a position to file its 65 ter documents to include pre-trial brief, witness list, and exhibit lists. At this time -- and again, assuming the Prosecution has some success with respect to the motions which I've just described for you -- the Prosecution anticipates calling between 12 and 18 witnesses in its case in chief. Again, assuming that we're able to rely upon judicial notice of adjudicated facts and transcripts pursuant to Rule 92 bis (D), the Prosecution expects its case in chief to last between two to four weeks, in total. Assuming the Defence is allocated approximately this same period of time, the Prosecution, Your Honour, anticipates this entire case to last between six and eight weeks. We would expect, given the time frame for the filing of the various document which is I've indicated, an opportunity for the Defence to respond, and at least with respect to Rule 92 bis (D), which anticipates the parties being heard, as well as 94(B), which similarly anticipates the parties being heard, the Prosecution would anticipate that by spring of next year this case would be ready to go to trial via a rather streamlined process again, assuming that the Prosecution is successful with respect to its submissions under the two Rules that I previously mentioned. So the Prosecution's position, Your Honour, is that this is a relatively short case, that pending resolution of pre-trial issues which the Prosecution will be filing shortly, this case will be ready to go in the springtime and will be a very streamlined case by the standards of the International Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. I should like to take advantage of this opportunity to invite you to cooperate with our extraordinary legal officers who have just joined the Tribunal. And I appreciate his professional qualities, as well as his personal ones, his character, and I should like to call upon both parties to cooperate with him. I'm talking about Mr. Harhoff, the senior legal officer, and that the conduct of this case and these proceedings, the pre-trial proceedings, in fact, I invite you to cooperate with him. And as far as I understand, there's a meeting today that has been scheduled. So I should like to invite the parties to attend the meeting, to get together perhaps somewhere where Mr. Harhoff will designate, in his offices or wherever. But that doesn't matter. It's the substance that counts. And I do hope that the parties will be fully aware of the fact that everybody wishes to see justice done, justice with a capital "J," which means that this calls for all of you to pull your efforts and see that we have justice and that justice is not only done but seen to be done. Justice must be seen to be done. Having said that, I should like to ask Mr. Stankovic if he has any observations to make, any comments perhaps at this point in time. Would you like to say anything, Mr. Stankovic? And you can feel free to say what you would like.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would like to ask that my case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slowly, please, Mr. Stankovic, to facilitate the work of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to have my case set aside from the other accused, severed. I don't want it to be linked to Kunarac, Kovac, and the other people, because the time period encompassed by the indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please speak slowly for the interpreters, Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will, Your Honour. So this period of time for which you charge me in the indictment, I should like to say that I never even knew those people, so I didn't know Kunarac or Kovac or the others, the rest of them. And from all this, I can draw one conclusion on the basis of what the Prosecutor said as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, this isn't the proper time to bring up the substance of the case. What I'm asking you now regards procedure. We're going to have ample opportunity to hear you at length. You'll have all the time you need to express yourself or through the intermediary of your Defence counsel. But what I would like to hear from you now is your health. How is your health? Is it -- are you in good health? Do you have any complaints?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Relatively good. Relatively good. I say "relatively" because who can say that he is fine when he's in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Detention isn't prison. Detention is detention, and there's a difference. Until proven guilty, so we can't call this "prison" yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If you're now embarking on those questions -- is it your intention to do this open session or in closed session this part of the proceedings? I've seen it done in both. I just wonder if Your Honour wants to deal with the accused's concerns, if any, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wish to deal with any questions with respect to protected persons or persons who enjoy protective measures, we can, of course, go into private session or closed session. Madam Registrar, which is it, private or closed? Is it the same thing?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Private. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Yes, partially? You asked for partially?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's just that I don't know what Your Honour's preference would be. But in some other cases I have seen the questions about the accused, concerns about prison or anything -- issues involving his health done in private session. I just didn't know whether we were going to be doing that in private session or open session. It matters not to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: No, no, it's open session. I can assure you. [Interpretation] And I think that it is important for everybody, not only those of us in this courtroom but elsewhere - I see that there are people in the public gallery - but if you wish to go into private session for anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. I think that that concludes our task for today. If nobody has anything to add -- Defence counsel, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for now, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. On that point I declare the meeting closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: at 3:38 p.m.
